SLICE E CLOSED CLEANLY. Bead closed and ALL TEN RESERVATIONS RELEASED IN ONE 'mote done' -- new-engineer now holds zero, and recall/graph.scala, wire.scala, the WOG suites and the embed-grakern integration suite are all free.

SECOND POPULATION: THREE OF SIX CLOSED. A (embed-bench Gold), B (core atlas types), E (recall RecallGraph). D2 is active with scout. C and D1 remain stalled at 115 minutes; checkpoint 17:25Z.

RULE 3 HAS NOW WORKED END TO END TWICE TODAY, and I want it on the record because I wrote it after breaking it. The rule: the chief must not close a bead holding another actor's live reservations, because 'mote done' -- which closes and releases together -- has an owner-only release half, so the only close available to me is the one that ORPHANS. Both times I ran who-has, found the paths held, recorded progress instead of closing, and asked the author to 'done' it. Both times they did, and nothing was orphaned.

The contrast is the measure of it: this morning I closed a bead with 'mote close' after landing, orphaned six reservations I could not release, and blocked this same foundational P1 for seventy minutes. Same situation this afternoon, ten reservations instead of six, zero orphans.

That is the whole value of writing down a rule you have just broken -- not that you remember the lesson, but that the next person does not have to relearn it from the same seventy minutes.
